theory: A document is a human-readable claim about checked mathematical artifacts, and being compiled is only one independent property of it. Completion obligations, reference diagnostics, source quotations, and publication ordering keep the displayed account tied to the source and evidence actually saved.
instead_of: Accept any PDF produced with exit code zero as a finished result; that would overlook missing references, altered quotations, and a publication whose source was never committed.

absorption.rationale: Additional known references or literal theorem environments fit the scanners, while general TeX macro expansion exceeds their explicitly bounded reading of executed and quoted text.

world_mapping.rationale: Obligations, compilation status, reference diagnostics, and controlled writeup fields separate what the document says from what Lean established.

abstraction.rationale: Pure completion and syntax functions accept gathered facts, while compilation owns the commit-before-publication ordering; another caller can reuse either without taking over the other.

justification.rationale: The code gives concrete reasons for rejecting transforming verbatim options, checking dropped glyphs, and publishing only after source persistence succeeds.

honest_limits.rationale: Compilation is explicitly unsandboxed and trusted-output-only; the document scanners name their limits rather than claiming to interpret arbitrary TeX.

rehearsals.requirement: Recognize another compiler diagnostic for unresolved citations.
rehearsals.why: The reference parser and diagnostic reporting already own this class of obligation.

rehearsals.requirement: Refuse a save after compilation when the source write fails.
rehearsals.why: LatexTools.check accepts the commit callback before it publishes outputs.

rehearsals.requirement: Establish completion for arbitrarily generated TeX conditionals and macro expansions.
rehearsals.why: The present scanner tracks supported literal execution shapes and explicitly stops short of being a TeX engine.
